summary: The note surveys architectural history from the Great Pyramid of Giza through Roman engineering, Gothic cathedrals, Renaissance domes, the Industrial Age skyscraper, Modernism, sustainable design, and digital tools like CAD, BIM and VR. Each era is tied to a speaker or event, such as conferences, lectures, a podcast and expos held between 2023 and 2026. It concludes that architecture reflects human history and rests on mathematics, physics, materials science and aesthetics.
one_line: A chronological tour of architectural eras from ancient pyramids to digital design, each linked to a recent lecture, conference or publication.
key_facts: Dr. Emily Harris unveiled a study on October 3rd, 2023 at the International Conference on Ancient Civilizations in Athens about the construction of the Great Pyramid of Giza, built around 2580–2560 BCE.
The pyramids were built using star alignment, geometry and local limestone and granite, with laborers moving stones without the wheel using sledges, ramps and manpower.
Marco Giuliano lectured on September 15th, 2024 at the Rome Architectural Summit on Roman aqueducts, viaducts and the Colosseum.
The Colosseum was erected in 80 A.D. and used vaults and arches to support large crowds and allow tens of thousands of spectators to exit swiftly.

Lillian Peterson's podcast "Structures of the Sky" (released November 12th, 2023) described Gothic innovations at Notre Dame Cathedral in Paris: pointed arches, flying buttresses and ribbed vaults from the 12th century.
Francesca Romano spoke at the Florence Festival of Arts on September 29th, 2023 about the dome of Florence's Cathedral, designed by Filippo Brunelleschi and completed in 1436.
Brunelleschi's dome used a herringbone brick pattern and a double shell with space in between to provide stability and reduce weight, plus purpose-designed construction machines.
Sandra Clark's work "Iron, Steel, and Stone" (December 1st, 2024) explored how iron and steel led to new forms like the skyscraper.
The Home Insurance Building in Chicago, built in 1885, is often considered the world's first skyscraper, using a steel frame.

Jameson Keeler spoke at the Modernism Exhibition on September 7th, 2025 about Le Corbusier, Frank Lloyd Wright and Ludwig Mies van der Rohe, who favored a "Less is more" approach with reinforced concrete, glass and steel.

The Global Green Building Expo on October 22nd, 2025 discussed eco-friendly materials and energy-efficient designs; architect Maya Kunis is cited as a leader, with photovoltaic glass and green roofs reducing carbon footprint.

At the Digital Architecture Forum on January 9th, 2026, experts showed how CAD and BIM are revolutionizing architecture, while VR lets builders walk through structures before construction and digital tools improve structural analysis.
